exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 1 and 2, set up the initial simplex tableau for the given linear programming problem.

problem.paragraph: $$\begin{matrix} \text{Maximize} & 22 x_{1} & + & 14 x_{2} & & \\ \text{subject} \text{to} & 3 x_{1} & + & 5 x_{2} & \leq & 30 \\ & 2 x_{1} & + & 7 x_{2} & \leq & 24 \\ & 6 x_{1} & + & x_{2} & \leq & 42\end{matrix} \text{and} x_{1} \geq 0 , x_{2} \geq 0.$$ ﻿

exercise_group.instruction: For each simplex tableau in Exercises 3–6, do the following:

problem.paragraph: Determine which variable should be brought into the solution.
Compute the next tableau.
Identify the basic feasible solution corresponding to the tableau in part (b).
Determine if the answer in part (c) is optimal.

exercise_group.instruction: Exercises 7–12 relate to a canonical linear programming problem with an $$m \times n$$ coefficient matrix $$A$$ in the constraint inequality $$A\textbf{x} \leq \textbf{b}$$ . Mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) A slack variable is used to change an equality into an inequality.
(T/F) A solution is called a basic solution if $$m$$ or fewer of the variables are nonzero.
(T/F) A solution is feasible if each variable is nonnegative.
(T/F) The basic feasible solutions correspond to the extreme points of the feasible set.
(T/F) If one of the coordinates in vector $$\textbf{b}$$ is negative, then the problem is infeasible.
(T/F) The bottom entry in the right column of a simplex tableau gives the maximum value of the objective function.

exercise_group.instruction: Solve Exercises 13–18 by using the simplex method.

problem.paragraph: $$\begin{matrix} \text{Maximize} & 10 x_{1} & + & 12 x_{2} & & \\ \text{subject} \text{to} & 2 x_{1} & + & 3 x_{2} & \leq & 36 \\ & 5 x_{1} & + & 4 x_{2} & \leq & 55\end{matrix} \text{and} x_{1} \geq 0 , x_{2} \geq 0.$$ ﻿

$$\begin{matrix} \text{Maximize} & 5 x_{1} & + & 4 x_{2} & & \\ \text{subject} \text{to} & x_{1} & + & 5 x_{2} & \leq & 70 \\ & 3 x_{1} & + & 2 x_{2} & \leq & 54\end{matrix} \text{and} x_{1} \geq 0 , x_{2} \geq 0.$$ ﻿

$$\begin{matrix} \text{Maximize} & 4 x_{1} & + & 5 x_{2} & & \\ \text{subject} \text{to} & x_{1} & + & 2 x_{2} & \leq & 26 \\ & 2 x_{1} & + & 3 x_{2} & \leq & 30 \\ & x_{1} & + & x_{2} & \leq & 13\end{matrix} \text{and} x_{1} \geq 0 , x_{2} \geq 0.$$ ﻿

$$\begin{matrix} \text{Minimize} & 12 x_{1} & + & 5 x_{2} & & \\ \text{subject} \text{to} & 2 x_{1} & + & x_{2} & \geq & 32 \\ & - 3 x_{1} & + & 5 x_{2} & \leq & 30\end{matrix} \text{and} x_{1} \geq 0 , x_{2} \geq 0.$$ ﻿
